end_to_end_latency.measurement: time from sending the demand_factor config request to receiving an /api/overview response whose total gateway-observed demand moved by more than max(10% of the low->high step, 0.25 A); served_change_ms is recorded only when served amps also moved by then, because served is capped by the lease budget (renewals never shrink a reservation)
end_to_end_latency.resolution_note: polled every 0.1s; each figure is an upper bound at that resolution plus one overview round trip and any dashboard caching (see max_observed_poll_gap_ms)

allocation_recovery_after_spike.criterion: every building 'active' with 1 <= reserved <= ceil(1.5 x demand) + 3 A; timeout 90s

limitations: Sampled state cannot prove absence of transients between polls.
Trials come from one run on one stack; stdev shows run-to-run spread, not independent samples.
Decision latency includes both accepted and rejected HTTP responses.
No gateway disk persistence, database failover, or physical breaker is evaluated.
